title: ac list prints ids, coverage and satisfied but never the criterion text, so a node planning from it is planning from ids -- and there is no ac show
body:
**`intent ac list` PRINTS ID, COVERING AT AND SATISFIED, AND NEVER THE CRITERION TEXT -- SO A NODE PLANNING FROM IT IS PLANNING FROM IDS.**

`ac: AC-04.6  covered-by: AT-04.6  satisfied: no` is the whole row. **There is no verb that prints a criterion's text**: `intent ac` has `list`, `status`, `satisfy`, `unsatisfy`, `gate`, `descope`, `rescope`, `withdraw`, `reinstate`, `new`, `edit` -- and no `show`. Reading a criterion means `jq` over `intent/.canon/st/<ID>.json`, which is the committed extract rather than the store, or opening the generated `acceptance.md`.

**MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, 2026-08-30.** vc built the v3.0.1 work-assignment plan by sizing four work packages from `ac list` and handed dc two glosses: `AC-04.6` as *hv's 1-1 file-form / lossless round-trip requirement* and `AC-05.7` as *the BATS conformance harness*. **`AC-04.6` is mutation completeness (D32) and `AC-05.7` is inert-argument detection. Neither gloss was close.** dc accepted them and spent a full shell-suite run before opening either row.

**THE ASSIGNMENT SURVIVED AND THAT IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A MITIGATION.** The sizing was right because it came from COUNTS, which `ac list` does print. What was wrong came from the field it does not print, and **nothing in the output signals that a field is missing** -- the row looks complete.

**WHY THIS IS A SURFACE DEFECT AND NOT A DISCIPLINE FAILURE** (dc's framing, adopted): a planning verb whose output omits the one field that says what the work IS invites exactly this, and the invitation is silent. The workaround -- `jq` into the canon extract -- also routes the reader to a RENDERING rather than to the store, which is a second defect the estate already tracks.

**REMEDY, NOT PRESCRIBED:** an `ac show <STID> <ACID>` mirroring `intent wp show`, or a `--text`/`--full` flag on `ac list`. `at list` has the same shape and the same gap for a test's note. **A row's text is the thing a criterion IS**, and it is currently the one part of it the CLI will not show you.

**REPORTED BY:** vc, 2026-08-30, after being the one who got it wrong; reframed from an error into a surface finding by dc.
